title: Milloin: answering with weekdays
focus: For on a named weekday, use the essive ending -na/-nä. Milloin sinä tulet? — Tulen maanantaina.
prerequisiteSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “When are you coming?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. For on a named weekday, use the essive ending -na/-nä. This ending marks the day of the event: maanantai + na gives maanantaina (“on Monday”). The question still begins with milloin. The complete question means “When are you coming”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking for the time + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.formation: Milloin asks for the time of an event.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Milloin te menette?”: choose “We are going on Wednesday.”
exercises.explanation: Use the complete weekday form after the supplied verb: Tulen tiistaina (“I am coming on Tuesday”). A short reply Tiistaina is natural. The ordinary weekday names in this lesson all take -na; do not add an English-style preposition. The complete reply means “We are going on Wednesday”.
